I've been growing chili on this land for decades. My plot is 2.2 mu — all chili, same as every year. My son works in the city now, so it's mostly me managing things. My knees aren't what they were, but I know this soil. I know when to water and when to wait.

I'll use seeds I saved from last year's strongest plants, like I always do. No sense buying expensive hybrid seeds from the shop — my seeds grow fine and I don't trust seeds I don't know. I'll rotary-till the field before planting, the way I've always done it. Gets the soil loose and warm.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at the base before transplanting, then add urea a couple times when the plants are growing. I don't use scales — I go by what looks right, what the village supply store recommends when I buy, and what worked last time. I'll irrigate from the well when the soil goes dry or before a hot stretch — probably five or six times over the season. Less if we get good summer rains.

Pests are the real trouble with chili. Aphids, sometimes mites, sometimes rot on the stems. I spray when I see a problem — four times usually gets through the season. I learned what to buy at the store from watching other farmers in the village.

I expect to get around 350 jin per mu — maybe a little more if summer is good. I sell most of it fresh at the township market.
